About this model

A voxel model of North Bayshore in Mountain View, California: the triangle between the Bayshore Freeway (US 101), Stevens Creek and San Francisco Bay that holds Google's main campus and Shoreline Park, plus Google's Bay View campus and part of NASA Ames on the far side of the creek. It is built from OpenStreetMap building footprints, roads, paths, parking, parks and water. Each cube is 3 metres; landmark models use cubes of 0.4 to 0.75 metres. The model stops about 70 metres beyond US 101, so only the first row of buildings on its far side is shown.

Footprints, tagged heights, roads, paths, parking, parks, water, solar arrays, street names, street addresses, mapped trees and mapped points (Stan, the Android statues, the Google sign and the artworks marked ◆) come from OpenStreetMap. Zoom in and every building named as Google's shows that name on its roof. Five of those names are not in OpenStreetMap and come from Wikimapia, matched by street address: Building 1875, Building SB45, Building SB55, Building SB65 and MTV 1245. Wikimapia's entries are undated and may be out of date. Seven more buildings on Shorebird Way and Charleston Road, east of Shoreline Boulevard, have no name on either map; they are marked as Google's on the word of this map's author and show their street number. Facade colours and windows, night lighting, the roof shapes of the amphitheatre tent, Gradient Canopy and the Bay View buildings, moving traffic, clouds, most trees and the small landmark models are illustrative. Buildings with no height tag use 4.5 m per mapped level, or two cubes (6 m) when no levels are mapped. About a dozen scattered buildings tagged Google have no card of their own; hover or tap one to see its mapped name, or use the Ownership lens to find them. In Fly and Walk, buildings and the landmark models are solid; on foot so are water, tree trunks, parked cars, planters and carport posts.

The ground is real terrain, stepped in half cubes (1.5 m): elevation from the Terrain Tiles open dataset on AWS (Terrarium tiles, about 4 m per pixel here). Each building stands on a level pad at the middle height of the ground under it, and lakes and ponds are level. No vertical exaggeration is applied.

Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database Licence. Rendering uses three.js (MIT licence). This is an independent fan-made model. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google; Google, Android and Googleplex are trademarks of Google LLC.
